title: American Family Insurance and AWS Team Up to Drive Innovation in the Insurance Industry
summary: American Family Insurance has selected AWS as its preferred cloud provider to accelerate its IT transformation, drive innovation, and improve customer experience. This multiyear agreement includes a co-innovation fund and initiatives to provide free cloud training in local communities and reduce environmental impact through cloud migration. The partnership aims to centralize IT infrastructure, reduce operating costs, and enhance responsiveness for American Family Insurance's 13.1 million policyholders.

title: Fubo Sports Network Now Available on Amazon Freevee
summary: Fubo Sports Network, the free-to-consumer TV network from FuboTV Inc., has expanded its reach by launching on Amazon Freevee. This move significantly increases its distribution to over 155 million devices, allowing fans to access live sports, original programming, and partner content. The network has seen substantial viewership growth and continues to add new series and content, aiming to connect with sports fans across various platforms at no additional cost.

title: Toll Brothers Apartment Living Announces Grand Opening of 323-Unit Haverly Luxury Apartment
summary: Toll Brothers Apartment Living has officially opened Haverly, a new 323-unit luxury apartment community in Phoenix, Arizona. The community offers a mix of studio, one, and two-bedroom floor plans with extensive indoor and outdoor amenities, including a resort-style pool, fitness center, and smart home technology. Located in Midtown Phoenix, Haverly provides convenient access to downtown, Sky Harbor Airport, and Tempe, catering to the region's strong economic and population growth.

title: Netflix’s strategy shift spurs worst-to-best comeback for stock
summary: Netflix has experienced a significant stock comeback due to its new strategy, primarily the introduction of a lower-priced, ad-supported subscription tier. This move, along with cracking down on password sharing, aims to attract new customers and retain existing ones amidst high inflation and increasing competition. Despite a 72% plunge earlier in the year, the stock has surged 84% since May, boosting investor and analyst confidence in the company's turnaround plan.

title: Amazon won't take down antisemitic film tweeted by Kyrie Irving, CEO says
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy announced that the company will not remove an antisemitic film from its platform, despite pressure to do so after Kyrie Irving tweeted a link to it. Jassy stated that Amazon must allow access to various viewpoints, even objectionable ones, citing a "slippery slope" in content moderation, though he personally finds parts of the film objectionable and is concerned about antisemitism. The film, "Hebrews to Negroes: Wake Up Black America!", contains false claims about Jewish control of media and Holocaust denial.

title: Hush appoints Sarah Miles as its new CEO
summary: Hush, a women's fashion and lifestyle brand, has appointed Sarah Miles as its new chief executive, effective January 16, 2023. Miles brings extensive experience from roles at Amazon, Diageo, and Sephora, and will lead Hush through its next phase of strategic growth. She replaces Kate Bartman, who will return to her previous role as chief trading officer after overseeing significant transformation and customer base growth.

title: Alibaba establishes beachhead in Spain
summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd has launched a new e-commerce platform called Miravia in Spain, targeting the local midrange to high-end consumption market. Miravia will operate independently, focusing on Spanish and European brands across various categories, and aims to cater to the needs of Spanish consumers while providing brands with sales and engagement tools. This move is part of Alibaba's strategy to expand into overseas markets and learn more about consumer demand in different regions amidst slowing domestic growth.

title: 40+ Spotify statistics 2026: SPOT stock, revenue and performance
summary: This article compiles over 40 statistics about Spotify (NYSE: SPOT) as of late 2022, detailing its market dominance, user growth, financial performance, and stock behavior. It highlights Spotify's leading market share in music streaming, its revenue model primarily driven by premium subscriptions, and its significant user base despite competition from tech giants. The report also touches upon Spotify's stock performance, including its all-time high and low, alongside insights into artist earnings and global user demographics.

title: Target gift card discount day 2022 is almost here. Get 10% off gift cards all weekend long
summary: Target is bringing back its annual gift card discount for the 2022 holiday season. Shoppers can get 10% off gift cards up to $500 this weekend, Saturday and Sunday, provided they are Target Circle members. The sale, which now lasts two days, offers a way to save on popular holiday presents, as gift card spending is projected to reach $28.6 billion this year.

title: Big Tech Antitrust Investigations: Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta/Facebook and Microsoft Updates
summary: This article provides an exhaustive overview of the ongoing antitrust investigations and regulatory scrutiny faced by major technology companies including Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta/Facebook, and Microsoft. It details numerous legal actions, fines, and inquiries across various countries and regions such as the EU, US, UK, Australia, India, and others, highlighting concerns over competition, data privacy, market dominance, and anti-competitive practices. The comprehensive list of updates serves as a running log of the global regulatory challenges confronting Big Tech since July 2020.

title: Business Matters: Central Mass. by the Numbers
summary: This article highlights several business developments in Central Massachusetts "by the numbers." It covers the reopening of Central Pizza in Southbridge after a two-year closure and $1 million investment, Amazon Data Services' $26.7 million property acquisitions in Grafton, Shrewsbury, and Westborough, and the reopening of The Red Baron Diner as Josh's Place at the Southbridge Municipal Airport. Additionally, it details a lawsuit against the Town of Westborough over the former Regal Cinemas property and the City of Worcester's $3 million minimum bid RFP for the Denholm Building.

title: Executives from eBay and Golden State Foods Join GS1 US Board of Governors
summary: GS1 US has elected Scott Gaffney from eBay and Brian Dick from Golden State Foods to its Board of Governors. These industry leaders will help guide GS1 US's strategy to enhance supply chain efficiency and visibility across various sectors, supporting members with digital transformation and demand planning. Their expertise is expected to be instrumental in optimizing supply chains to meet consumer needs.

title: Disney Advertising enhances clean room capabilities with VideoAmp partnership
summary: Disney Advertising is upgrading its data clean room technology through a partnership with VideoAmp, integrating measurement, planning, and optimization tools to help advertisers with audience-based matches across platforms. This move comes ahead of the Disney+ ad-supported tier launch and addresses the growing need for meaningful advertising measurements in connected TV and the deprecation of third-party cookies. The collaboration aims to provide advertisers with better insights into audience reach and frequency across Disney's properties, with initial brand tests already underway with Omnicom Media Group.

title: Warner Bros. Discovery Returns HBO Max to Amazon's Prime Video Channels | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery has returned HBO Max to Amazon's Prime Video Channels in the United States, reversing a previous decision made under AT&T ownership that resulted in a loss of 5 million subscribers. This move aligns with WBD CEO David Zaslav's strategy to make HBO Max as widely available as possible. The company is also working to combine HBO Max and Discovery Plus into a single streaming service, potentially named Max.

title: Adobe Cuts 100 Jobs Concentrated in Sales as Tech Tightens Belt
summary: Adobe Inc. has eliminated approximately 100 jobs, primarily in sales, as part of a broader trend of tech companies reducing expenses through staff cuts. While some affected employees were offered alternative roles within the company, Adobe's workforce reduction is significantly smaller compared to the thousands of jobs cut by other tech giants like Amazon and Meta. The San Jose-based software company had over 28,700 employees by the end of its fiscal third quarter.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) shares declined 0.20% on a generally poor trading day for the stock market, though the company still outperformed several key competitors like Amazon, Walmart, and Costco. Despite the daily loss, the stock broke a two-day winning streak and closed below its 52-week high. Trading volume was higher than its 50-day average.

title: Top Strategic Predictions for 2023 and Beyond
summary: Gartner's 2023 strategic predictions focus on "seizing uncertainty" to transform challenges into opportunities for organizations. The predictions cover themes such as virtual workspaces, labor volatility, pay equity, employee value metrics, sustainable AI, decentralized identity, citizen-led denial of service attacks, moonshot investments, cloud ecosystem consolidation, and sovereignty partnerships. The overarching message encourages flexibility, adaptability, and a willingness to embrace change to drive better outcomes.

title: Adobe Eliminates 100 Jobs in Sales, Joins Other Companies in Using Job Cuts to Reduce Expenses
summary: Adobe Inc. has eliminated 100 jobs in its sales division, aligning with other tech companies reducing expenses through workforce adjustments. Despite these cuts, Adobe stated it is not undergoing company-wide layoffs and is still hiring for critical roles, reassigning some affected employees to support "critical initiatives." The company's adjustments are significantly smaller compared to thousands of job cuts reported by other tech giants this year.

title: Racine Sues Amazon for Stealing Delivery Drivers’ Tips
summary: D.C. Attorney General Karl A. Racine has filed a lawsuit against Amazon.com Inc. and Amazon Logistics, Inc. for allegedly stealing tips from delivery drivers. The lawsuit claims that Amazon deceived consumers into believing their tips would go entirely to drivers, but instead diverted a significant portion to cover labor costs and increase profits, in violation of the District's Consumer Protection Procedures Act. The OAG is seeking civil penalties and a court order to prevent Amazon from continuing these practices, emphasizing the importance of fair wages for workers and transparency for consumers.

title: Amazon CEO adds 4 'S-team' members after losing key executives
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy has appointed four new vice presidents to the company's senior leadership team, known as the 'S-team'. This expansion comes after Jassy has seen five members depart since he took over in July 2021, with a sixth executive also expected to leave soon. The article highlights the significant changes in Amazon's top executive ranks under Jassy's leadership.

title: First Circuit Affirms Food Delivery Drivers Must Arbitrate Misclassification Claims | Insights
summary: The First Circuit Court of Appeals has affirmed that food delivery drivers for Postmates and Grubhub must arbitrate their misclassification claims. The court ruled that these couriers are not engaged in interstate commerce under Section 1 of the Federal Arbitration Act (FAA), as their deliveries are considered local and distinct intrastate transactions, even if the goods originated interstate. This decision aligns the First Circuit with other courts that have determined local delivery drivers are not exempt from arbitration under the FAA.

title: For HPE, The Cloud Is A Private And A Public Matter
summary: HPE is focusing on its GreenLake utility platform to expand its presence in the hybrid cloud market, emphasizing private cloud offerings. The company aims to make its entire portfolio available as a service and is seeing steady growth in GreenLake's orders and revenue. HPE is enhancing GreenLake with new services like Private Cloud Enterprise and expanding partner offerings, catering to businesses that prefer a mix of public and private cloud solutions, especially for edge computing needs.

title: HPE GreenLake Adds AWS’ Kubernetes Service and Other Hybrid Cloud Capabilities
summary: HPE GreenLake Private Cloud Enterprise has expanded its availability worldwide and is introducing new hybrid cloud capabilities. These enhancements include support for Amazon Web Services’ Kubernetes software and an improved analytics tool for measuring both private and public cloud usage and costs. The updates aim to provide greater flexibility and control for enterprises managing hybrid cloud environments, further solidifying HPE's as-a-service model for on-premises solutions.

title: HPE GreenLake For Private Cloud Packs New AWS Kubernetes Punch
summary: HPE has enhanced its GreenLake for Private Cloud Enterprise platform, notably integrating with AWS’ Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Anywhere. This expansion offers significant new services opportunities for partners and allows customers to deploy AWS Kubernetes in various private cloud environments. The updates also include new analytics for multi-cloud consumption, six new workload-optimized instances, and planned integrations with other Kubernetes platforms like Red Hat OpenShift.

title: What kind of company do the striking HarperCollins workers face?
summary: This article examines the corporate structure, ownership, and political affiliations of HarperCollins, the company facing a strike by its workers in New York. The authors describe HarperCollins as a highly profitable entity owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, highlighting Murdoch's history of anti-worker actions and extensive political connections. The piece suggests that HarperCollins workers can empower their struggle by understanding the company's background and by forming a democratically controlled rank-and-file committee to fight for their demands, linking their struggle to broader working-class movements.

title: AWS, Google, Microsoft and Oracle all get a piece of the Pentagon's $9B JWCC cloud computing contract
summary: The Pentagon has awarded Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle shared portions of a $9 billion Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) contract, which will run through 2028. This multi-vendor approach replaces the previously controversial single-award JEDI contract and aligns with industry best practices of using multiple cloud providers for resilience and cost management. Analysts view this distributed award as a positive step, promoting competition and allowing the DOD to leverage the best capabilities of each cloud provider.

title: Amazon.com Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) shares rose by 0.24% to $88.46 on a day when the broader market saw declines, ending a four-day losing streak. The stock's performance outpaced major competitors like Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet. Amazon closed significantly below its 52-week high, with trading volume also below its 50-day average.

title: Washington DC sues Amazon over withheld delivery driver tips
summary: The District of Columbia is suing Amazon.com Inc and its subsidiary, Amazon Logistics, alleging they withheld tips from delivery drivers using the Amazon Flex service. Attorney General Karl Racine stated that Amazon diverted tips to reduce its own labor costs and increase profits, tricking consumers into thinking they were compensating drivers. This lawsuit follows a 2021 settlement where Amazon paid $61.7 million to drivers after a similar investigation by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.

title: Pentagon Divides Big Cloud-Computing Deal Among 4 Firms (Published 2022)
summary: The Pentagon awarded lucrative cloud-computing contracts, potentially valued at up to $9 billion, to Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Oracle. This decision marks a significant shift from an earlier attempt to award a sole contract to Microsoft, which was later scrapped after legal challenges and a recognition that the department's needs had evolved. The new Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability project aims to provide comprehensive cloud services across all security domains and classification levels for the Defense Department.

title: Shane Jones
summary: Nature's Sunshine Products, Inc. has appointed Shane Jones as its new Chief Financial Officer. Jones brings over 25 years of experience in the finance sector, including senior roles at Amazon and 1-800 Contacts, and will be a key member of the company's executive committee, focusing on efficiency and profitable growth. Terrence Moorehead, Nature’s Sunshine President and CEO, highlighted Jones's proven track record in building high-performing teams and achieving business objectives.

title: Google, Oracle, Amazon, Microsoft to share $9 billion ‘return of JEDI’ defense contract
summary: Google, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft will jointly share a $9 billion hybrid contract from the Pentagon to provide secure cloud services globally. The contract, known as Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability, is scheduled for completion by June 8, 2028, with work to be performed in Reston, Va. This agreement follows previous discussions and changes regarding the Department of Defense's cloud computing needs.

title: Brad Miller Joins Moderna as Chief Information Officer
summary: Moderna, Inc. has announced the appointment of Brad Miller as Chief Information Officer, effective January 3, 2023. Miller will join Moderna's Executive Committee, reporting to CEO Stéphane Bancel. He takes over from Marcello Damiani, the current Chief Digital Officer, who will be retiring in March after seven and a half years with the company.

title: Amazon Games and Bandai Namco Online Bring Blue Protocol to the West in 2023
summary: Amazon Games and Bandai Namco Online Inc. are bringing "Blue Protocol," a free-to-play, anime-inspired online action RPG, to Western markets in the second half of 2023 for PC, Xbox Series X|S, and PlayStation 5. A Closed Beta for PC is planned earlier in the year. The game features character customization, five unique classes, and a story about saving the world of Regnas from destruction using a mysterious light called Flux.

title: Amazon seeks dismissal of class action over penalizing workers who take time off for military service
summary: Amazon has requested the dismissal of a class-action lawsuit alleging they penalized employees who took time off for military service, violating the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA). The company claims one plaintiff was inadvertently fired and another was unqualified for promotion, while highlighting its status as a major employer of military service members. This case is part of a broader legal trend, as a similar lawsuit against American Airlines also addresses USERRA violations regarding military leave compensation.

title: ‘Flipping Out’ star Jeff Lewis buys LA estate for $5.92M
summary: Television personality and interior designer Jeff Lewis, known from Bravo's "Flipping Out," has purchased a new Spanish-style chateau in LA's Hancock Park neighborhood for $5.92 million. This acquisition comes shortly after he sold his Hollywood Hills property for $5.2 million. The 7,366-square-foot home features six bedrooms, original 1920s details, and landscaped grounds with a pool, departing from the modern style of his previous residence.

title: JD.com’s Ochama Expands Pick Up Points to 120+ with Physical Stores in Europe
summary: Ochama, JD.com’s B2C omni-channel retail brand in Europe, has expanded its pick-up point network to over 120 locations across Germany, Belgium, France, and the Netherlands. This expansion allows customers in Germany and Belgium to now access fresh and frozen foods. Ochama leverages JD.com's automated warehousing and global supply chain to offer competitive prices and next-day fulfillment, collaborating with third-party offline channels like Blokker stores for pick-up points.

title: Playing Catch Up With Big Tech In Antitrust Regulation
summary: This article examines the evolving landscape of antitrust regulation in India, focusing on how the Competition Commission of India (CCI) is adapting to challenges posed by big data, internet commerce platforms, and disruptive technologies. It traces jurisprudential trends through several key cases involving cab aggregators (Ola-Uber), hotel aggregators (OYO, MakeMyTrip, Goibibo), instant messaging apps (WhatsApp), e-commerce giants (Flipkart, Amazon), and the Android ecosystem (Google). The author highlights the CCI's shift from a price-centric approach to considering non-price factors and the complexities of regulating nascent digital markets while fostering innovation.

title: Pentagon splits $9 billion cloud contract among Google, Amazon, Oracle and Microsoft
summary: The Pentagon awarded $9 billion worth of cloud computing contracts to Google, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, and Oracle. These Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) contracts will provide enterprise-wide cloud services across all security domains and classification levels until 2028. This move signifies the military's shift towards utilizing multiple vendors for its cloud computing needs, learning from past litigation that halted a single-vendor IT modernization project.

title: Pentagon awards multibillion-dollar cloud contract to Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle
summary: The Pentagon has awarded a multibillion-dollar cloud computing contract, Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC), to Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Oracle. This move diverges from a previous single-vendor approach (JEDI contract) that faced legal challenges from Amazon alleging interference by former President Trump. The new multi-vendor contract, worth up to $9 billion, aims to provide resilient and cost-effective cloud services for the military, enabling access to sensitive data globally.

title: Grabango taps Kroger veteran Ken Fenyo as CMO as it looks ahead to supermarkets
summary: Grabango has appointed former Kroger executive Ken Fenyo as its first Chief Marketing Officer, aiming to leverage his grocery industry experience as the company expands its frictionless-checkout technology beyond convenience stores to supermarkets. Fenyo's role will focus on helping food retailers understand the immediate benefits of Grabango's computer vision-based technology, which has been tested in a 40,000-square-foot supermarket. This move comes as Grabango prepares to compete with other frictionless checkout providers, including Amazon.

title: US warehouse development to hit 7-year low in 2023, Prologis says
summary: US warehouse development is projected to hit a 7-year low in 2023 due to higher capital costs, leading to a 60% year-over-year decline in development starts according to Prologis. This reduction in supply, coupled with strong e-commerce demand, is expected to drive rent growth above 10% next year. The forecast also predicts shifts in leading markets, with Texas surpassing California in logistics warehouse demand and Mexico experiencing record warehouse demand due to nearshoring.

title: Why Are Quantum Computing Stocks Falling?
summary: This article examines the struggling performance of pure-play quantum computing stocks—IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS)—all of which went public via SPAC mergers. Despite the immense potential of quantum computing, these companies are experiencing significant stock value declines and revenue shortfalls compared to their initial projections. The piece highlights that while major tech companies like IBM are heavily investing in quantum R&D, current revenue generation for specialized quantum firms remains modest, largely driven by Quantum Computing as a Service (QCaaS) and government contracts.

title: More Stores Do Double Duty as Distribution Centers for Online Orders
summary: Retailers are increasingly utilizing their physical stores as mini distribution centers to fulfill online orders, alongside traditional warehouses. This strategy aims to accelerate deliveries, optimize inventory management, and leverage existing brick-and-mortar locations more efficiently. For example, Ulta Beauty now packages orders from 116 of its stores to speed up shipping.

title: Is Amazon employing a deceptive strategy to keep its Prime members subscribed?
summary: Amazon is accused of using deceptive tactics to make it difficult for Prime members to cancel their subscriptions, a process code-named "Iliad" which significantly reduced cancellations. The cancellation process involves navigating multiple pages, trick questions, and attractive offers. Both the Federal Trade Commission and the Norwegian Consumer Council have received complaints and launched investigations into Amazon's methods.

title: E Ink expects more growth next year
summary: E Ink Holdings Inc (元太科技), the sole global e-paper display supplier, anticipates continued business growth next year, driven mainly by the increasing adoption of electronic shelf labels (ESLs) by large US retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, and Amazon. Despite potential recession risks, the company expects its ESL segment to achieve its fastest growth, following strong performance this year where ESLs became its primary revenue source. E Ink also identifies e-notes and electronic labels for packing boxes, particularly in Europe due to new reuse regulations, as future growth engines.

title: Experts devised a technique to bypass web application firewalls (WAF) of several vendors
summary: Claroty researchers have developed a technique to bypass web application firewalls (WAFs) from multiple vendors by using JSON syntax in SQL injection payloads. This method exploits the WAF's inability to parse JSON syntax appended to SQL statements, enabling malicious code to bypass detection. The technique was successfully tested against WAFs from vendors like Cloudflare, F5, Imperva, Palo Alto Networks, and Amazon Web Services (AWS).

title: Watch Out For TuringBots: A New Generation Of Software Development
summary: TuringBots, AI-powered software coined by Forrester, are revolutionizing software development by augmenting human capabilities across planning, design, building, testing, and deployment. While not replacing human developers, these tools significantly enhance efficiency and intelligence in the software development lifecycle. Organizations are advised to understand the technology, adopt strategic implementation for tester and coder TuringBots, and stay informed through ongoing research to navigate this evolving landscape.

title: Google merges Waze with Maps in effort to streamline and cut costs
summary: Google is merging its Waze team with its Maps service, a move aimed at streamlining operations and cutting costs without planned layoffs. This comes amidst a challenging macroeconomic environment that has impacted other major tech companies, leading to layoffs and hiring freezes. The article also provides a technical analysis of Google's stock (GOOG.us), suggesting a potential bullish trend based on hourly EMAs and stochastic indicators.

title: Amazon pilots returns at Staples stores
summary: Amazon is piloting a program that allows customers to return products at select Staples stores, expanding its physical touch points for returns. This initiative builds on Amazon's existing partnerships with retailers like Kohl's and Whole Foods for return drop-offs, addressing the high rate of e-commerce returns. This expansion could add about 1,000 more return locations for Amazon across 45 states if fully implemented.

title: Arqit announces QuantumCloud™ powered by AWS
summary: Arqit Quantum Inc. announced that its QuantumCloud™ platform is now powered by Amazon Web Services (AWS) and available on Amazon S3. This integration allows AWS customers to access Arqit's quantum-safe encryption service, enhancing data security for a broad audience. Traxpay is highlighted as an example customer already leveraging this technology for secure digital finance instruments.

title: Will TNT Walk Away From The NBA?
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav's recent comments questioning the necessity of the NBA for TNT have sparked industry speculation about the future of their 33-year partnership. As the NBA seeks significantly increased media rights—potentially $50 billion to $75 billion—from incumbents TNT and ESPN, the possibility of tech giants like Amazon entering the bidding process looms. While an NBA-TNT divorce seems unlikely due to their deep integration and the network's commitment to "Inside the NBA," the evolving media landscape and WBD's cost-cutting measures could lead to a reevaluation of the relationship, possibly involving a split package with streaming services.

title: New Technique Discovered To Bypass Web Application Firewalls (WAF) Of Several Vendors
summary: Cybersecurity experts at Claroty have developed a new generic method to bypass Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) from multiple leading manufacturers. This technique was discovered while researching a SQL injection flaw in Cambium Networks' wireless device management platform. The bypass abuses the default JSON syntax support in SQL engines to craft new, less common SQLi payloads that can evade WAF detection.

title: Popular WAFs Subverted by JSON Bypass
summary: Web application firewalls (WAFs) from major vendors like AWS, Cloudflare, F5, Imperva, and Palo Alto Networks are vulnerable to a JSON bypass technique, allowing attackers to obfuscate malicious SQL commands. Claroty researchers discovered that these WAFs fail to detect SQL commands embedded in the JSON format, enabling attackers to access and modify database data. The affected vendors have been notified and have updated their products to include JSON syntax support, but experts advise additional security layers beyond WAFs.

title: HPE GreenLake fortified with new cloud services
summary: HPE has enhanced its GreenLake edge-to-cloud platform with new application, analytics, and developer services, aiming to bolster its position in the hybrid cloud market. These updates, announced at HPE Discover 2022, include expanded container deployment options for Kubernetes with Amazon EKS Anywhere, enhanced consumption analytics, and broadened partner ecosystem integrations with Red Hat OpenShift and VMware. An early access program for HPE GreenLake for Data Fabric and HPE Ezmeral Unified Analytics was also introduced to modernize analytics and data management.

title: Music now has over 616 million paying streaming subscribers globally
summary: Global music streaming services had 616.2 million subscribers by mid-2022, an increase of 17.6% year-over-year, according to Midia Research. While growth slowed slightly compared to the previous year, notably due to macroeconomic pressures and the maturation of Western markets, the industry remains resilient with significant contributions from emerging markets like China. Spotify continues to lead the market, though its share has gradually declined as competitors like Tencent Music Entertainment, Amazon Music, and YouTube Music gain ground.

title: As Market Dynamics Pivot, Alpha Opportunities Are Set to Improve
summary: The U.S. equity market is shifting from an environment favoring passive strategies to one that is more conducive for active managers. Historically, during periods of extreme market concentration, low volatility, and low dispersion of returns, active managers often underperformed. However, as these extremes unwind—driven by factors like slowing economic growth, inflation, and rising interest rates—opportunities for active stock picking and alpha generation are expected to improve significantly.

title: Rivian, Mercedes pause plans for JV to build electric vans in Europe
summary: Rivian and Mercedes-Benz have announced a pause in their plans for a joint venture to produce electric vans in Europe. This decision comes after Rivian secured a significant order to supply 100,000 electric delivery vans to Amazon by 2030, with a pilot program already underway in the U.S. The article also touches upon broader automotive industry news, including trade tariffs and dealership transactions.

title: IBM Remains Big Tech’s Disaster
summary: The article portrays IBM as a struggling legacy technology company that has failed to keep pace with its Big Tech counterparts. Despite its historical dominance, IBM missed critical opportunities in personal computing and cloud computing, leading to a significantly smaller market capitalization and lower revenue compared to industry leaders like Microsoft and Apple. Wall Street analysts maintain a "Hold" rating, with price targets below its current trading price, suggesting a bleak outlook for the company's future performance.

title: WaveDancer Offers Visibility and Security to Global Supply Chains
summary: WaveDancer, Inc. announced the launch of its new website showcasing Maverix, a commercial blockchain-enabled supply chain management platform. Maverix offers enhanced visibility, security, and traceability for global supply chains by leveraging blockchain's immutable ledger technology. The platform, initially developed for a U.S. Intelligence agency, aims to solve common supply chain problems like data silos and lack of trust through its modular, secure, and AI/ML-enhanced architecture.

title: Rivian Scraps Plan to Make Electric Vans in Europe With Mercedes
summary: Rivian Automotive Inc. has scrapped its plans to jointly build electric vans in Europe with Mercedes-Benz AG, just three months after signing a memorandum of understanding. CEO RJ Scaringe stated that focusing on its consumer and existing commercial businesses represents the most attractive near-term opportunities for Rivian. This decision marks another setback for Rivian's global ambitions and follows a previous abandoned partnership with Ford Motor Co.

title: Microsoft invests $2 billion in London Stock Exchange cloud deal
summary: Microsoft is acquiring a 4% stake in the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) for $2 billion, marking a significant cloud partnership between the two entities. This deal aims to integrate Microsoft's applications with LSEG's products, broaden its customer base, and explore shifting trading activities to the cloud. The move highlights the increasing convergence between Big Tech and financial services, drawing scrutiny from regulators concerned about concentration risks in cloud providers.

title: Here's What Kroger Was First Called
summary: This article details the history of Kroger Co., from its origins as the Great Western Tea Company in 1883 to its current status as one of America's top grocers. It highlights the determination of its founder, Bernard "Barney" Kroger, through early challenges like floods and financial setbacks, and explains how his innovative approach to retail, such as one-stop shopping and self-sourcing, set precedents for future supermarkets.

title: ElectraMeccanica Celebrates Commissioning Of New Manufacturing Facility And Corporate Headquarters In Mesa
summary: ElectraMeccanica Vehicles Corp. celebrated the commissioning of its new manufacturing facility and corporate headquarters in Mesa, Arizona, marking its official establishment as an American OEM. The facility is expected to produce up to 20,000 vehicles annually and create 200-500 new jobs, bolstering Arizona's manufacturing industry. This move supports the production of their flagship all-electric SOLO and SOLO Cargo vehicles, with the company emphasizing the importance of partnerships with local and state governments for economic development.

title: How did big-box retailers fare during the week of Black Friday 2022?
summary: During Black Friday week 2022, Walmart outperformed Target and Best Buy in year-over-year sales growth. All three major big-box retailers, Walmart Inc (NYSE: WMT), Target Corporation (NYSE: TGT), and Best Buy Co, Inc (NYSE: BBY), experienced greater year-over-year growth in their online sales compared to their retail sales. Best Buy saw a decline in sales, contrasting with the modest growth at Walmart and Target, potentially due to decreased demand for electronics.

title: The Honest Company Names CPG Veteran Carla Vernón as CEO
summary: The Honest Company has appointed Carla Vernón, a former Amazon and General Mills executive, as its new CEO, effective January 9, 2023. Vernón will become one of the few Afro-Latina chief executive officers at a US publicly traded company, focusing on category growth and profitability while continuing the company's mission of conscious living. This leadership transition follows current CEO Nick Vlahos's nearly six-year tenure, during which he led the company's IPO and expanded its brand.

title: A New Amazon Returns Location: Staples
summary: Amazon has launched a pilot program allowing customers to return items at select Staples stores, similar to its existing partnership with Kohl's. This initiative provides customers with another convenient, often free, option for returns, potentially adding 1,035 new drop-off locations if the program expands nationally. For Staples, this partnership could drive foot traffic and increase potential sales as customers enter stores for returns.

title: Naver Webtoon, digital comics case for global MBA study
summary: INSEAD, a leading business school, has published a case study on Naver Webtoon, highlighting its success in transforming the comics industry and becoming a global storytelling platform. The study positions Naver Webtoon as a textbook example of Blue Ocean Strategy due to its innovative business model and creation of new market opportunities. The company leveraged localization and intellectual property to rapidly expand its global user base.

title: At Macy’s, a Digital Marketplace Is Born
summary: Macy's has launched a new digital marketplace to expand its e-commerce capabilities, allowing it to quickly add new brands and categories from third-party sellers with minimal inventory risk. The initiative, developed in under a year with assistance from Mirakl and Deloitte Digital, aims to provide a seamless customer experience and create more profitable relationships.
